To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the uncoupling effect of 2, 4-dinitro-phenol (and of other uncouplers) is due to a large increase of the effective conductance of the protonmotive force barrier of the cristae membranes, and that this large increase of conductance is the direct consequence of a large increase of proton permeability of the cristae M phase.

the uncouplers of oxidative phosphorylation catalyse a rapid and reversible proton conductance of their own across the membrane system and thus short-circuit the chemi-osmotically driven proton current.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which uncouplers cause the uncoupling of oxidation and phosphorylation.
the characterization of the proton current across the membrane system, and with the mechanism whereby uncoupling agents short-circuit this current.
the measurement and interpretation of proton conductance across the membrane system in suspensions of ratliver mitochondria under a variety of conditions of protonmotive force.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

2,4-DNP or FCCP, when added in the normal uncoupling range, causes a large increase of the effective membrane proton conductance and thus short-circuits the protonmotive force and uncouples the phosphorylation process from oxidation.
the uncoupling agents act by a direct increase in the proton conductance of their M phase, which is the membrane system of the cristae.
the uncoupler causes a large increase of the effective conductance of the proton current across the membrane system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the titratable protons of the inner aqueoous phase of the liver-mitochondria are titrated by the circulating protons, the effective rate of titration depending on the protonmotive force of the M phase and the effective proton conductances of the M phase.

the proton current across the M phase of rat-liver cristae membrane is the driving force for the respiratory chain, and the uncoupling effect of 2, 4-dinitro- phenol (or carbonly cyanide p-tri- fluoromethoxyphenyhydrazone) is to be accounted for by a large increase of the effective conductance of the proton current across this membrane.

The main takeaway from our work is that
uncouplers increase the rate of titration across the inner membrane of mitochondria.
the proton conductance of mitochondria is not constant.

the M phase of mitochondria is a proton conductor and that the proton conductance of this phase is regulated by the uncoupling action of the proton ionophore, 2,4- dinitrophenol, and related compounds.
